notes: The only open case was an SD with no RECORD clause (R1 X(5), R2 X(2)). The refuter called 1985 silent; it is not: §1985:II.2.1.4.3 makes fixed-or-variable the implementor's choice when no RECORD clause is given, and GR1's 'size of each data record is completely defined in the record description entry' is the sentence §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR13-GR15 pair with an implementor-chosen FIXED format 3, so it does not force variable length. Under the documented fixed choice every record is 5 characters (II.2.1.4.1), RELEASE R2 releases the 5-character area 'ABXXX', and RETURN INTO W X(5) moves that 5-character current record: [ABXXX] then [CCCCC], as observed. Attack point: whether II.2.1.4.3's 'file description entry' reaches an SD; XI.3.2.4 GR2 makes the SD's RECORD clause the Sequential I-O one, and §1985:XI.4.4.4 GR13 itself speaks of a sort file that 'contains only fixed length records'. kb/Work PB5386: a receiver whose subscript or reference modifier is lowered to a 15.4 temporary (a function-identifier, a division, an item read through a shared REDEFINES area) was identified in the hoist before the statement; it is now identified at its store by its identification bracket (ExpressionBinder.ResolveReceivingAtStore), witnessed by cases/14.9.34-RETURN/pb5386_return_into_subscript_after_return.

next.reason: Same two-step equivalence: RETURN, then an implicit MOVE that does not occur if the RETURN was unsuccessful, with 'alphanumeric group move' for RECORD VARYING. The record size, which 1985 takes from 'rules specified for the RECORD clause', is §2023:13.18.43.4 GR16. Difference: 1985 fixes only the timing of 'subscripting associated with identifier-1'. 2023 fixes all of it: 'Item identification of the data item referenced by identifier-1 is done after the record has been read' (§2023:14.9.34.4 GR5), which covers reference modification, already legal in 1985 and with unstated timing there.
